extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students in analysis / measure theory
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter excerpt developing Lebesgue and Borel measures on RN (definitions, uniqueness, regularity, relation to Riemann integral), properties of diadic cubes, translation/dilation invariance, measure-zero characterizations, and basic properties of convolution with Lp estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Borel sets (R1 and RN)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Borel sets of R1 are the members of the smallest σ-algebra containing the elementary sets (finite disjoint unions of bounded intervals); equivalently the smallest σ-algebra containing the open sets or the compact sets. Similarly define BN for RN as the smallest σ-algebra containing all compact (or open) sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every open or compact set is Borel; open intervals generate B1 because every interval is a countable intersection of open intervals; compact sets generate B1 because closed bounded intervals are compact and every interval is countable union of closed bounded intervals. For RN, either open geometric rectangles or compact geometric rectangles can be used to generate BN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric vs abstract rectangle; product measure on RN
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish geometric rectangle (N-fold product of bounded intervals) and abstract rectangle (product of measurable sets as in Fubini's theorem). Lebesgue measure on RN is constructed so that the measure of a geometric rectangle equals the product of the lengths of the sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction can be done inductively using Fubini or by grouping variables differently; both constructions yield same measure. This product-property is used later for uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.1 — product σ-algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: If m and n are integers ≥ 1 then Bm × Bn = Bm+n (within Rm × Rn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: open sets in the product are countable unions of open geometric rectangles of the form U × V with U open in Rm and V open in Rn; this shows each side contains the other. This proposition shows the σ-algebra for Lebesgue measure on RN is independent of grouping of coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Borel measure on RN
rubrics_metrics.description: A Borel measure on RN is a measure on the σ-algebra BN of Borel sets that is finite on every compact set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such measures will have the key property of regularity (Theorem 6.2) and include Lebesgue measure as a primary example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.2 — regularity of Borel measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Borel measure µ on RN is regular: for any Borel set E, µ(E) = sup{µ(K): K ⊆ E, K compact} = inf{µ(U): U ⊇ E, U open}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses two topological facts for RN: (i) existence of increasing sequence of compact sets whose union is RN; (ii) for any compact K there exist decreasing open sets Un with ⋂Un = K. The theorem is proved by approximating E from inside by closed/compact sets and from outside by open sets, with explicit ε-control and closure under complements and countable unions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation of compact indicator by C_c functions (iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K is compact then there exists a decreasing sequence of real-valued members of C_c(RN) with pointwise limit the indicator function of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct continuous functions fn ∈ C_c(RN), 0 ≤ fn ≤ 1, with fn ≡ 1 on K and fn ≡ 0 off a shrinking open neighbourhood; then replace by min{f1,...,fn} to make them decreasing. Used in proving uniqueness results (Corollary 6.3) and density statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.3 — uniqueness from integrals of C_c
rubrics_metrics.description: If µ and ν are Borel measures on RN such that ∫ f dµ = ∫ f dν for all continuous functions on RN of compact support, then µ = ν (agree on all Borel sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: approximate indicators of compacts by decreasing C_c functions and apply dominated convergence; use Theorem 6.2 to extend equality from compacts to all Borel sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.4 — density of C_c and generation of Lp
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) C_c(RN) is dense in L^p(RN, µ) for 1 ≤ p < ∞. (b) The smallest closed subspace of L^p(RN, µ) containing all indicator functions of compact sets is L^p itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the approximating sequence for compact indicators (iii), dominated convergence and Proposition 5.55/5.56 to conclude density and that indicators of compacts generate L^p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diadic cubes and their properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer n ≥ 0 and integer tuple (a1,...,aN) define the diadic cube Qn(a1,...,aN) of side 2^{-n} by {x: 2^{-n} aj < xj ≤ 2^{-n}(aj+1) for 1≤j≤N}. The collection Qn partitions RN; for each x the cubes Qn containing x are nested with Qn ⊇ Qn+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cubes are used to produce countable partitions of RN at different scales and serve as building blocks to approximate open sets and determine measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 6.5 — open sets are union of diadic cubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any open set in RN is the countable disjoint union of diadic cubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given open U, for each x ∈ U choose the smallest-scale diadic cube contained in U; the construction yields a countable disjoint collection whose union is U. This fact is used to determine measures from diadic-cube values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.6 — Borel measures determined by diadic cubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Borel measure on RN is determined by its values on all the diadic cubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values on diadic cubes determine values on all open sets (Lemma 6.5), and Theorem 6.2 then determines values on all Borel sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.7 — existence and uniqueness of Lebesgue measure
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a unique Borel measure on RN for which the measure of each geometric rectangle is the product of the lengths of the sides; this measure is the N-fold product of 1-dimensional Lebesgue measure (Lebesgue measure on RN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness follows from Proposition 6.6 and the fact that geometric rectangles can be decomposed into diadic cubes; existence comes from the product construction (iterated Lebesgue measures or Fubini-based construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.8 and Corollary 6.9 — Borel maps and homeomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If F: RN → RN0 is a Borel function then F^{-1} maps BN0 into BN; in particular any homeomorphism of RN carries BN to BN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to component functions Fj which are Borel measurable; this implies translations and dilations are Borel/homeomorphic operations on sets, functions, and measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action of translations/dilations on measures and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: For translation τ_{x0}(x)=x+x0, define τ_{x0}(E)=E+x0, τ_{x0}(f)(x)=f(x+x0); similarly for dilation δ_c(x)=c x. These operations map Borel sets to Borel sets and induce corresponding operations on Borel measures by pushforward: τ_{x0}(µ)(E)=µ(τ_{-x0}E). Integration respects these operations: ∫ f d(τ_{x0}µ)=∫ τ_{-x0}f dµ, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These relations are verified first for indicators and simple functions and extended by monotone convergence/density arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.10 — translation invariance and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Lebesgue measure m on RN is translation invariant: τ_{x0}(m)=m for every x0 in RN. Moreover, Lebesgue measure is the unique translation-invariant Borel measure on RN that assigns measure 1 to the diadic cube Q0(0,...,0). Effect of dilation: δ_c(m) = |c|^{-N} m, i.e., ∫ f(cx) dx = |c|^{-N} ∫ f(x) dx for nonnegative Borel f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness proof: diadic cubes at each scale are translates of each other so their measures are fixed by the single value on Q0; apply Proposition 6.6. Dilation scaling follows similarly from how diadic cube sizes change under scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.11 — Riemann = Lebesgue for continuous on rectangles
rubrics_metrics.description: For a continuous function on a compact geometric rectangle, the Riemann integral equals the Lebesgue integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to 1-D case and compute by iterated integrals: Corollary 3.33 for Riemann and Fubini + product construction for Lebesgue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.12 — characterization of Lebesgue measure-zero sets
rubrics_metrics.description: In RN, the Lebesgue measurable sets of measure 0 are exactly the subsets E with the property: for any ε>0, E can be covered by countably many geometric rectangles of total volume < ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: if E has that covering property, approximate by unions En of rectangles with m(En)<1/n to get measure 0. Conversely, if E is Lebesgue measurable and m(E)=0, reduce to bounded case and apply product σ-algebra arguments and Proposition 5.38/5.40 to cover E by geometric rectangles with arbitrarily small total volume (careful doubling argument near the end).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: Borel vs Lebesgue measurable sets and Fubini
rubrics_metrics.description: Borel measurable sets are independent of measure, whereas completions (Lebesgue measurable sets) depend on the measure; there exist Lebesgue measurable subsets of RN not in the product σ-algebra of Lebesgue measurable sets of factors. Hence use caution when combining Fubini's theorem and Lebesgue measurability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: some Lebesgue measurable functions need to be adjusted on a null set to become Borel measurable; Problem references provided for non-Borel Lebesgue-measurable examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of convolution f * g
rubrics_metrics.description: For suitable functions on RN, (f * g)(x) := ∫_{RN} f(x-y) g(y) dy (equivalently ∫ f(y) g(x-y) dy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonnegative Borel functions f,g the convolution is a Borel function by composing continuous and Borel maps and applying Fubini. For general (signed/complex) functions define via decomposition into nonnegative parts when integrals are finite a.e., otherwise set to 0 where undefined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.13 — commutativity and associativity of convolution
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonnegative Borel functions on RN, (a) f*(g*h) = (f*g)*h and (b) f*g = g*f (associativity and commutativity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Fubini's theorem and change of variables; Theorem 6.10 (translation invariance) is used in computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.14 — Lp convolution inequalities (Young-type)
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonnegative Borel f,g the convolution is finite a.e. and satisfies norm bounds in the following cases: (a) f∈L^1, g∈L^1 ⇒ ||f*g||_1 ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_1. (b) f∈L^1, g∈L^2 ⇒ ||f*g||_2 ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_2 (and symmetric). (c) f∈L^1, g∈L^∞ ⇒ ||f*g||_∞ ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_∞ (and symmetric). (d) f,g∈L^2 ⇒ f*g defined a.e. and ||f*g||_∞ ≤ ||f||_2 ||g||_2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use Minkowski's inequality for integrals, translation invariance of Lebesgue measure, and the Cauchy–Schwarz (Schwarz) inequality; arguments apply also when functions are signed/complex by working on absolute values and decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.15 — convolution commutes with translations
rubrics_metrics.description: For all suitable f,g and t∈RN, τ_t(f*g) = (τ_t f) * g = f * (τ_t g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify by direct substitution in the integral definition together with translation invariance of Lebesgue measure; check on integrable Borel functions and extend by density.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.16 — continuity of translations in Lp (p<∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ L^p(RN) with 1 ≤ p < ∞, then translation is continuous in the translation parameter: lim_{h→0} ||τ_h f - f||_p = 0. (Continuity fails in general on L^∞.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: first show for g ∈ C_c using dominated convergence, then approximate arbitrary f by C_c functions using Corollary 6.4a and use triangle inequality to transfer continuity to f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 35 — existence of ultrafilters (Zorn's Lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Zorn's Lemma to show that every filter is contained in some ultrafilter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard maximality argument: partially order filters by inclusion, apply Zorn to chains to obtain maximal (ultra)filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 36 — existence of filter generated by family
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonempty class F of subsets of X is contained in some filter iff no finite intersection of members of F is empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for extendability to a filter: finite intersection property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 37/38 — characterization of ultrafilter
rubrics_metrics.description: A filter F is an ultrafilter iff for every subset A⊆X, either A ∈ F or A^c ∈ F (equivalently maximal among filters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the usual maximality characterization: if a filter has the property that for every A either A or its complement is in the filter, it cannot be properly extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 39 — correspondence between {0,1}-valued additive set functions and ultrafilters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonzero additive set functions defined on the set of all subsets of X taking values in {0,1} stand in one-to-one correspondence with ultrafilters on X: the ultrafilter consists exactly of the sets on which the set function equals 1. The set function is a measure iff the corresponding ultrafilter is closed under countable intersections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives linkage between finitely additive {0,1}-valued measures and ultrafilters; complete additivity corresponds to countable-intersection-closure of ultrafilter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 40 — existence of nontrivial ultrafilter on infinite X
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is infinite then X has a nontrivial ultrafilter; hence there exists a nonnegative additive set function µ on P(X) assuming only values 0 and 1 that is not a point mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct free ultrafilter using Zorn or ultrafilter lemma; yields finitely additive 0–1-valued measure not concentrated at a single point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 41 — no countably complete ultrafilter on Z+
rubrics_metrics.description: The set Z+ of positive integers has no nontrivial ultrafilter closed under countable intersections; equivalently the {0,1}-valued finitely additive µ from previous problem is not a (countably additive) measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows limitation: there are no nonprincipal ultrafilters on N that are σ-complete, so the corresponding 0–1 additive set functions are not measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 42–43 — integration without complete additivity (monotone convergence caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider an integration theory where complete additivity is dropped: µ is a nonnegative additive set function on a σ-algebra with µ(X) < ∞. Many properties of the integral before the Monotone Convergence Theorem remain true except that E ↦ ∫_E f dµ is only additive, not completely additive; thus some corollaries and converses (e.g., part of Corollary 5.23 and Corollary 5.24) fail. Problem 42: for nonnegative f, standard simple approximations s_n converge uniformly if f is bounded. Problem 43: using 42 show that for bounded measurable f,g, ∫_E(f+g) dµ = ∫_E f dµ + ∫_E g dµ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These problems explore which parts of integration theory survive when σ-additivity is weakened to finite additivity; use uniform convergence of simple approximations for bounded f to retain linearity for bounded measurable functions.
